rows.gics_industry: Independent Power and Renewable Electricity Producers
rows.key_quote: Vistra reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.767 billion, up over 30% year-over-year from $1.35 billion, driven by generation gains from higher realized prices, PJM capacity revenues, and retail contributions. The company reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $6.8-$7.6 billion and expects to deliver at or above the midpoint. Management announced a founding investment of up to $1 billion in Helix Digital Infrastructure with KKR, NVIDIA, and KIA, and maintained its 2027 EBITDA opportunity range despite lower ERCOT forward curves.

MBIA reported a narrower adjusted net loss of $7 million in Q2 2026, compared to $8 million a year earlier, driven by lower loss expenses at National. National's PREPA exposure decreased by $35 million to $390 million, and the oversight board increased its settlement offer to about $3 billion, but bondholders dismissed it as inadequate. Holding company liquidity declined to $337 million, and book value per share fell to negative $45.58. Management is cautiously monitoring PREPA litigation and potential sale options, with no new guidance provided.

DraftKings reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $115 million, exceeding expectations despite customer-friendly sports outcomes and higher customer acquisition spend. Revenue growth was strong with sports handle up 11% YoY and sports consumer volume up 15%, while customer acquisition surged 75% at the best CAC since Q1 2025. The company's predictions offering saw volume grow from $2.3 billion to $11 billion annualized between April and July, with over 600,000 customers engaged. Full-year guidance is maintained at $6.5-$6.9 billion revenue and $700-$900 million adjusted EBITDA, with core business on track for ~$1 billion adjusted EBITDA.

Ellington Financial reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with GAAP net income of $0.43 per share and adjusted distributable earnings of $0.60 per share, exceeding the dividend. Book value increased and annualized economic return was 13.6%. Longbridge originations rose 38% year-over-year, with record proprietary reverse mortgage volumes and strong securitization execution. The company maintained momentum with portfolio growth, expanding credit hedges, and a pending acquisition, while also enhancing disclosures.

VAALCO reported Q2 2026 net income of $42.4 million and adjusted EBITDAX of $54.8 million. Production increased in Gabon to over 9,300 boepd, and Baobab resumed production in June with rates slightly above pre-startup forecast. The company raised full-year production guidance, expanded Egypt drilling to 10-15 wells with no CapEx increase, and maintained CapEx in line with guidance. Management expressed confidence in continued growth into H2 2026 and beyond.

Emera reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EPS of CAD 0.69, down CAD 0.10 year-over-year, with year-to-date adjusted EPS of CAD 2.06, consistent with last year. The company is on track for compound annual adjusted EPS growth above the 5%-7% target through 2026 and within that range through 2030. The New Mexico Gas sale received regulatory approval and is expected to close later this month, with after-tax proceeds of CAD 650-700 million. Management highlighted strong performance at Peoples Gas and progress on data center opportunities in Tampa Electric, while noting lower earnings at New Mexico Gas and higher corporate interest costs.

Essent Group reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $190 million or $2.08 per diluted share, up from $1.82 last quarter and $1.93 a year ago, with an annualized ROE of 13.4% and book value per share of $63.01 growing nearly 13% year-over-year. The mortgage insurance in-force grew 1.2% year-over-year to $249.7 billion, persistency was 84%, and the default rate was stable at 2.53%. The reinsurance segment saw net premiums written jump to $249 million in H1 2026 from $31 million in H1 2025, with the combined ratio at 77.9% for the quarter, and management maintained its 2026 P&C written premium guidance of approximately $320 million. Capital returns were strong with $350 million in share repurchases year-to-date and a quarterly dividend of $0.35 per share declared.

Fidus reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted NII of $0.50 per share, down from $0.62 in Q1, covering the base dividend. Total investment income was $43.5 million, a $4 million decrease quarter-over-quarter due to lower fee income. The company realized $6.4 million in net gains from equity monetizations and exited Virtex non-accrual with a $11 million realized loss, leaving no non-accruals. Management sees deal flow picking up in the second half, citing improved activity levels and a healthy portfolio with 6% EBITDA growth.

Fluor reported Q2 2026 revenue of $4.3 billion, up 9% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA up to $149 million from $96 million and adjusted EPS of $0.91 versus $0.43. New awards exceeded $6 billion, backlog grew to $26.9 billion, and management raised expectations for full-year book-to-bill above 1. The quarter included $44 million in additional losses on the Gordie Howe project, and guidance implies a small step-up in second-half EBITDA, with most of it already in backlog.

Galiano Gold reported Q2 fiscal 2026 production of 34,400 ounces, bringing first-half output to 69,000 ounces, near the upper end of guidance. Revenue was $156.6 million, adjusted EBITDA $78.5 million, adjusted EPS $0.09, with AISC of $2,473 per ounce, within guidance. Full-year guidance was maintained at 140,000-160,000 ounces and $2,300-$2,600 AISC. The company continued investing in Nkran Cut 3 pre-stripping and exploration at Esaase and Abore, with a planned hedge roll-off and higher-grade ore expected to improve results in 2027 and beyond.

Global Partners reported a strong Q2 2026 with net income of $71 million versus $25.2 million in the prior year, and adjusted EBITDA of $148.2 million versus $98.2 million. Fuel margins improved significantly, and all segments contributed to growth. The company redeemed preferred units at a high cost of capital and maintains strong balance sheet with leverage at 2.85x. Management remains confident in the business despite volatile refined product markets and expects the backwardated curve to increase future inventory carrying costs.

Granite Ridge reported Q2 2026 production of 32,044 BOE/d and Adjusted EBITDA of $79.6 million, up from $75.4 million a year ago. GAAP EPS was $0.23, up from $0.19, while adjusted EPS was $0.09. Guidance for full-year LOE was raised to $8.25-$9.25 per BOE, and production is expected to trend toward the lower end of the range. Management reiterated its 2027 free cash flow inflection with strong exit production nearing 40,000 BOE/d and improving gas realizations.

Wendy's Q2 FY2026 global systemwide sales declined 6.5%, with U.S. same-restaurant sales down 7.0% and traffic down 12.5%, partially offset by a 5.6% average check increase. The company withdrew its full-year outlook and reduced its dividend. Management acknowledged quality degradation, weakened value proposition, inconsistent operations, and ineffective marketing, outlining five strategic focus areas but providing no specific turnaround details until next quarter.

GSBD reported Q2 FY2026 NII of $0.38 per share (annualized yield on book value ~12.6%) and NAV of $12.06 per share, down from $12.17. Declared a Q3 base dividend of $0.32 and a supplemental dividend of $0.03, bringing trailing 12-month dividends to $1.54. Net debt-to-equity was 1.35x at quarter end, below target of 1.25x post quarter end, and management plans to reactivate share buybacks. Non-accruals improved to 2.9% (from 3.2%), with a net reduction in non-accrual companies to 10. New commitments were modest at $12.9 million, with a wide spread increase of 511 bps versus six months ago. Management noted subdued M&A activity, but a pickup post quarter end, and remains selective in deployment.

Gray Media reported Q2 2026 total revenue of $839 million, beating the high end of adjusted guidance by about $9 million with 9% YoY growth. Political revenue surged to $83 million, well above the $60-70 million guidance range. Core advertising was down 1%, better than the mid-single-digit decline guided. The company raised Q3 political guidance to $165-185 million and expects strong Q3/Q4 with political cash flows used for debt reduction. Leverage improved to 5.73x total net leverage, and the board authorized up to $250 million for debt repurchases.

HEI reported Q2 2026 core EPS of $0.13, down from $0.20 a year ago, with utility core net income down to $32.6 million from $42.5 million. Results included a non-cash gain from remeasuring the Maui wildfire settlement liability, but core operations were hurt by higher interest expense, O&M costs, and lower interest income. Management reiterated FY2026 O&M headwinds, including no further deferral of wildfire costs and expected PIM/SSM losses, while progressing on rate rebasing and securitization of WMP costs. The company received credit upgrades from S&P and Moody's, but faces regulatory uncertainty around JERA's proposed regulated GenCo and a large new generation RFP.

Hamilton reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $144M (21% annualized ROE) with a combined ratio of 95%, pressured by $50M catastrophe losses, mostly from the Middle East conflict. Gross premiums grew 17% overall, with International up 22% and Bermuda up 12%. The company raised a modest $16M reserve charge on casualty lines and maintained full-year low double-digit growth guidance, while noting competitive property pricing but stable casualty rates.

IAMGOLD reported Q2 2026 gold production of 188,100 oz, bringing year-to-date output to 371,700 oz, tracking toward full-year guidance of 720,000-820,000 oz. Adjusted EBITDA reached $507.1 million and adjusted EPS was $0.42, up from $0.13 a year ago. The company generated $893.5 million in mine-site free cash flow year-to-date, repurchased over $500 million in shares, and ended with net cash. Côté is set to release an updated mine plan by year-end, targeting throughput expansion to 40,000 tons per day and a longer mine life.

Kodiak Gas Services reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $391 million, up 21% year-over-year, and record adjusted EBITDA of $217 million, up 22%. Compression Infrastructure grew revenue 7% year-over-year with adjusted gross margin of 70% and fleet utilization at 98.2%. The company raised full-year adjusted EBITDA, margin, and cash flow guidance reflecting improved visibility. Power Infrastructure segment generated $33 million revenue with 64.5% margin, and management highlighted a growing project pipeline, including a limited notice to proceed for a West Texas data center supply deal.

Kingstone reported record Q2 2026 results: net income of $15.5 million, diluted EPS of $1.05, and a GAAP net combined ratio of 70.2%, improving 1.3 points. Direct premiums written grew 19% to $72.5 million, with new business policy count up 35% and retention up 2 points. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, noted a softening market and increased competition, and highlighted a strengthened reinsurance placement with 14% more capacity and lower core cat costs. Capital returns accelerated with a 20% dividend increase and ongoing buybacks.

Kimbell Royalty Partners reported a record Q2 2026 with oil, natural gas, and NGL revenues exceeding $100 million for the first time, and record consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $84.9 million. Average daily production hit 25,830 BOE/d, with run-rate increasing to 26,967 BOE/d after the Mesa acquisition. Distribution raised 15% to $0.47 per unit, and guidance for 2026 is affirmed, with an update expected after the drop-down acquisition closes. Management remains active in M&A, noting Permian competition is intense but that they are selective and disciplined.

In Q2 FY2026, Loma Negra reported cement volumes down 1.4% YoY and consolidated revenue up 2.1% to ARS 238.1 billion. Adjusted EBITDA fell 2.5% to ARS 48.2 billion, with margin down 97 bps to 20.2%. Net profit improved to ARS 7.5 billion from ARS 0.5 billion a year ago, helped by lower financial losses. Management noted soft April volumes due to heavy rains, maintained a cautiously optimistic outlook for H2, and highlighted new RIGI projects and road concessions as potential supports.

Main Street Capital reported strong Q2 2026 results with an annualized ROE of 18.9%, significant NAV per share increase driven by net fair value gains, and another material realized gain from the Centre Technologies exit of over $46 million. The company declared a $0.30 supplemental dividend and raised regular monthly dividends by 3.9% to $0.265 per share for Q4 2026. Management remains optimistic about future realizations and portfolio growth, though notes increased variability among portfolio companies and a cautious dividend income outlook from some companies.

Dauch reported Q2 2026 sales of $2.96B and adjusted EPS of $0.32, with adjusted EBITDA of $389.6M (13.2% margin). The company raised the low end of full-year guidance for sales to $10.6B-$10.8B and adjusted EBITDA to $1.36B-$1.425B, citing strong first-half performance. Synergies reached $70M run-rate savings, on track for $100M+ by year-end. Management expressed confidence in integration progress and future growth, noting strong demand on key platforms and a $2B quoting pipeline.

Docebo reported Q2 2026 with ARR re-acceleration for the second consecutive quarter, driven by broad-based strength across net new, expansion, and international. Management expressed high confidence in second-half acceleration, supported by lapping AWS and Dayforce headwinds (approx. $19M over next four quarters) and a strong FedRAMP pipeline. The company is investing in a foundational FDE team for agentic workflows and a healthcare vertical, following the prior government playbook. Cash position is $45M with $90M debt, and the SIB is expected to have minimal share tenders at current stock price; no major acquisitions planned in next 12 months.

In H1 2026, revenue grew 13.9% YoY to RMB 14.7 billion, with engine unit sales up 10.9%. Gross profit rose 36.5% to RMB 2.5 billion, and operating profit increased 58.9% to RMB 988.2 million. Net profit attributable to shareholders surged 53.2% to RMB 560.6 million. Management noted strong demand for high-horsepower engines, with AI data center sales reaching 1,800 units, and reiterated a full-year AIDC volume target of 3,500 units. The company raised its 2025 dividend to $0.87 per share and is planning capacity expansion to 5,000 units for high-horsepower engines.

Algonquin's Q2 2026 adjusted EPS was flat year-over-year at $0.04, with adjusted net earnings declining to $29.2M from $33.6M, largely due to higher financing costs and one-time items. The company reaffirmed its 2026 and 2027 adjusted EPS forecast and is progressing on multiple rate cases, including a favorable Missouri settlement and California WEMA proposed decision. Management also announced plans to redomicile to the U.S., expecting $0.02-$0.03 EPS benefit, and reiterated no equity issuance through 2027.

ACMR reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $292.9 million, up 36% YoY, with ECP and advanced packaging growing over 150%. Orders in H1 rose 105% YoY, and the company raised its full-year revenue guidance midpoint to $1.125-$1.175 billion, implying 25-30% growth. Gross margin was 46% and net cash exceeded $1 billion. The company also announced panel-level plating order wins and progress on PECVD and track platforms.

TDS Telecom delivered 66,000 fiber service addresses in Q2 2026, marking the strongest first-half delivery in company history, and raised full-year fiber address guidance to 250,000-300,000. Residential fiber net adds grew 47% YoY to 15,100. However, total telecom revenues declined 6% (4% ex-divestitures) and adjusted EBITDA was pressured by legacy copper and cable declines, leading to reduced total revenue guidance and narrowed EBITDA guidance. Array's cash site rental revenue rose 65% YoY, and it closed spectrum transactions with T-Mobile and Verizon, while the TDS offer for Array's minority interest remains under review.

Aflac reported adjusted EPS of $1.80 (excluding FX) for Q2 2026, up 1.1% year-over-year, with net EPS of $1.63. Japan sales fell 5.6% in the quarter but were up 7% for the first half, and the company expects full-year Japan sales to exceed 2025. U.S. net earned premiums grew 2.3%, but guidance for 2026 net earned premium growth was lowered to just below the 3%-6% range. Management raised its expected Japan benefit ratio to the high end of the 60%-63% guidance range, due to an unfavorable mix of lapses, and reaffirmed strong capital returns and strategic reinsurance expansion.

Assured Guaranty reported strong Q2 2026 results with adjusted operating income per share up 22% year-over-year to $1.23, driven by higher net earned premiums and lower loss expense. First-half PVP of $152 million was 48% higher than the prior year, led by U.S. public finance and global structured finance. Management remains confident in the pipeline, with $42 million of PVP already expected from Q3 transactions. Record adjusted book value and adjusted operating shareholders' equity per share were achieved.

Q2 FY2026 was exceptionally strong with total portfolio same-store NOI growth of 13.2% year-over-year and 12.7% for the first six months. Same-store occupancy held at 90.7% for Trilogy and SHOP same-store NOI grew 20.5% year-over-year. Management increased full-year guidance and highlighted over $1.4 billion in closed acquisitions year-to-date with $800 million more expected by year-end, none of which is reflected in revised guidance. Net debt to EBITDA stood at 2.5x, indicating continued deleveraging.

AIG reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.00, up 10% YoY, with adjusted after-tax income of $1.1 billion. Underwriting income rose 10% to $686 million, and the accident-year combined ratio improved 30 bps to 88.1%. Net premiums written grew 9% (11% ex-North America property), with global commercial up 9%. Management remains on track for sub-30% expense ratio by 2027, but is cautious on property pricing pressure, reducing Lexington retention by 9 points. Capital returned to shareholders was $904 million including $641 million in buybacks.

AMR reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $25.6 million, down from $30 million in Q1, with 3.5 million tons shipped. The company lowered its full-year shipment guidance by 1 million tons to a range of 14.2-15.4 million tons and raised its cost guidance midpoint by $7 to $103-$107 per ton, citing higher diesel and supply costs, weaker met coal markets, and reduced DTA terminal capacity due to storm damage. Management noted continued weak global steel demand and tightness in the Australian PLV spread, while highlighting the ramp-up of the new Wildcat low-vol mine as a positive mix shift.

Amrize reported strong Q2 2026 results with revenue growth of 8.6% and organic growth of 6.7%, driven by mega projects in data centers, energy, and infrastructure. Adjusted EBITDA grew 5.8% to $986 million, net income up 14.4%, and adjusted EPS up 8.6%. The company faces oil-driven cost inflation and higher freight rates, but expects price over cost gap to improve in H2 and turn positive in Q4. Full-year guidance was maintained, reflecting confidence in margin recovery. Capital returns included $502 million to shareholders, with a $1 billion buyback program and a quarterly dividend of $0.11 per share.

ANI Pharmaceuticals reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $266M (up 26% YoY) and record adjusted EBITDA of $71.6M (up 32% YoY). Cortrophin Gel revenue was $117.1M, up 43% YoY and 56% QoQ; management revised full-year Cortrophin guidance modestly to $520-540M, still representing 50-55% growth. The gout sales force expansion is fully operational with strong leading indicators, and generics revenue grew 10% YoY. The company reiterated total revenue guidance of $1.1B and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $285-300M.

Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was $72M, down from $76.9M in the prior year, but first-half Adjusted EBITDA rose 14% to $123M. Same-store merchandise sales ex-cigarettes fell 0.9% while merchandise margin expanded 110 bps to 34.7%. Announced a strategic acquisition by subsidiary APC to acquire U.S. Petroleum Partners for $205M plus $30M in earnout stock, expected to add ~280 million gallons and ~$30M annual Adjusted EBITDA, closing later this year. Management reiterated confidence despite a challenging consumer and fuel price environment.

Casella Waste Systems reported Q2 2026 revenue of $543.7 million, up 16.9% year-over-year, beating the prior guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $123.2 million, up 12.5% year-over-year, with margin down 80 basis points to 22.7%. Revenue guidance was raised by $30 million, but adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow, and operating cash flow guidance were reaffirmed. Management highlighted strong pricing, landfill volume growth, and M&A integration, but noted fuel and resource solutions margin headwinds.

AdvanSix reported Q2 2026 sales of $421 million, up 3% year-over-year on 18% favorable pricing, offset by a 15% volume decline. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $32 million (down $24 million year-over-year) and adjusted EPS declined to $0.19 from $1.24. The company offset $72 million of raw material cost inflation with pricing, but Plant Nutrients volumes were weak due to farmer economics, and guidance implies a greater-than-usual seasonal headwind in the third quarter. Management still expects second-half earnings and cash flow improvement, with $45Q credits and CapEx reductions supporting cash.

Atmus delivered record Q2 FY2026 sales of $528 million, up 16.4% year-over-year, driven by the Koch Filter acquisition and Power Solutions growth. Adjusted EBITDA was $109 million (20.7% margin), and EPS was $0.82, beating prior-year $0.75. The company narrowed full-year EBITDA guidance to 19.75%-20.25% and maintained EPS guidance at $2.85-$3.00, while noting second-half headwinds from Middle East conflict and moderating pricing/FX.

Consolidated Q2 production of ~204,000 oz in line with expectations; adjusted net income was $41M ($0.03/sh) with ~$71M realized losses from gold collar contracts. Fekola, Masbate, and Otjikoto outperformed, while Goose was impacted by the April crusher fire. The Menankoto Exploitation Permit was granted, clearing the way for Fekola Regional pre-stripping. 2026 production guidance narrowed to 820-920k oz, cash cost guidance unchanged, AISC guidance lowered; management expects meaningful free cash flow improvement in H2 and into 2027 as prepaid contracts are complete.

CGBD reported Q2 2026 NII of $0.35 per share, fully covering the new base dividend, with total investment income of $62 million down from the prior quarter due to lower OID accretion and fee income. NAV per share fell to $15.61 from $15.89, partly due to $24 million in net realized and unrealized losses, including markdowns on SPF and US Infra. Management expects Q2 to be the earnings trough and anticipates increased earnings and supplemental dividends over the next four to six quarters as JVs ramp. Platform originations reached $1.5 billion, up over 20% quarter-over-quarter, but M&A activity remains muted due to geopolitical and macro uncertainty.

Calumet reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $175 million, with strong performance in both Specialties and Montana Renewables despite planned turnarounds. The company deleveraged below 4x restricted group leverage, repurchased $115 million of notes and terminated a sale-leaseback. Management guided to accelerated deleveraging, announced a novel MaxSAF 150 second-phase expansion to reach 120-150 million gallons of SAF by spring 2027, and identified ~$50 million of low-risk specialty growth capital for 2027-2028.

Concentra reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $606 million, up 10% YoY, with core revenue up 8% excluding acquisitions. Adjusted EBITDA grew 22.5% to $140.9 million, with margin expansion of ~240 bps to 23.3%. Adjusted EPS increased ~40% to $0.52. Management raised or reiterated guidance, noted strong organic growth in Onsite Health Clinics, and announced a CEO succession. Leverage fell below 3x, and the company continued buybacks and dividends.

Chesapeake Utilities reported Q2 2026 adjusted net income up 5% and adjusted EPS of $1.05, also up 5% year-over-year (1% EPS increase). The company raised full-year 2026 capital guidance by $100 million to $550-$600 million and announced the $1.2 billion Florida Energy Pathway Project. Management reaffirmed long-term growth and expects to provide 2027-2031 capital and earnings guidance in February 2027. Customer growth remains above national averages but showed signs of slowdown.

Claritev reported Q2 2026 revenue of $257.5 million, up 6.6% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $155.8 million (60.5% margin), with operating cash flow up 51% to $93 million. Bookings were strong at $30 million ACV in Q2, bringing H1 to $70 million, up 150% YoY, and the company raised its full-year bookings target to $100 million. Guidance was raised, and management expressed confidence in achieving at least 50% ACV bookings growth for the year.

CareTrust REIT reported record Q2 2026 investments of approximately $900 million at a blended 8.9% yield, leading to record revenues, normalized FFO per share of $0.51 (up 19% YoY), and a raised full-year 2026 guidance to $2.03-$2.06 normalized FFO per share. The pipeline remains strong at $540 million with additional investments closed post-quarter, and the balance sheet is highly liquid with net debt to EBITDA at 1.0x. Management expressed strong confidence in continued growth across skilled nursing, SHOP, and U.K. care homes.

Mobility Global reported Q2 FY2026 organic revenue growth of approximately 7%, modestly below expectations, with CARFAX growing 8% and B2B growing 4%. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 43%, reflecting disciplined cost management. Due to first-half top-line performance, full-year revenue guidance was lowered to 6.9%-7.7% growth. Management noted adjustments to the go-to-market approach and softer non-U.S. automotive activity as key factors.

Groupon reported Q2 2026 billings and revenue each down 1% YoY, falling slightly short on the top line, but adjusted EBITDA finished at the high end of guidance and free cash flow was a positive $15 million. The top-line shortfall was concentrated in North America Local, while organic channel revenue returned to growth and managed channel revenue grew strong double digits. Management guided Q3 billings growth of 4%-6% and maintained full-year outlook, citing July momentum with mid-single-digit growth and continued AI-driven initiatives.

Runway Growth Finance reported Q2 2026 total investment income of $37.0 million and net investment income of $18.2 million, up from $29.5 million and $10.6 million in Q1 2026. Total investment portfolio fair value increased 35% to $1.2 billion following the SWK acquisition. Management emphasized portfolio diversification, improved risk ratings (weighted average risk rating down to 2.34 from 2.67), and strong credit quality, highlighting a 76% historical recovery rate. They expressed confidence in the portfolio's fundamentals and repurchase plans despite a disconnect from market pricing.

Plains All American reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $738 million, up significantly from Q1, and maintained full-year guidance of $2.88 billion ±$75 million. Management raised 2026 growth capital to $400-$450 million, increased Permian production growth outlook to 100-200 kb/d exit-to-exit, and expanded Cactus III by 75 kb/d to 725 kb/d. Leverage was reduced to 3.3x following the Canadian NGL sale, with $1.75 billion in expected free cash flow for 2026. The tone is optimistic about 2027 momentum and macro tailwinds from Middle East volatility.

Petrobras reported record Q2 2026 results, with recurring net profit and gross profit at all-time highs, despite Brent not being at its historical peak. Production reached 2.7 million barrels of oil per day, up 15% YoY, and refinery utilization surpassed 100%, helping reduce imports by 40% and increase exports by 12%. Adjusted EBITDA was $20 billion, up 70% QoQ and nearly double YoY. Management highlighted production capacity still to ramp up (270,000 bpd) and reaffirmed capital discipline, with no change to guidance.

Q2 revenue was $271 million, in line with guidance, while medical-only revenue rose 4% sequentially to $222 million. Gross margin was 60% company-wide and 63% for medical-only, with adjusted EBITDA of $98 million (36% margin). Cash balance was $325 million with $53 million operating cash flow. Management raised CapEx guidance by $10 million, noting growth in Georgia and Texas, and flagged positive patient growth trends in Florida, Georgia, and Pennsylvania.

Park Hotels & Resorts reported Q2 2026 results that exceeded expectations, with total portfolio RevPAR up nearly 6% to $217 and ex-Royal Palm up nearly 7%. Adjusted EBITDA increased nearly 9% to $204 million, margins expanded 80 bps, and adjusted FFO per share was $0.70. Group revenue grew 9.5% and leisure transient grew over 13%, with strong performance in Hawaii, Florida, and urban markets. The company raised its full-year guidance, with RevPAR now expected at $225, EBITDA at $735 million, and adjusted FFO per share at $2.58-$2.66.

Take-Two delivered Q1 FY2027 net bookings of $1.39 billion, slightly above guidance of $1.32-$1.37 billion, driven by NBA 2K and GTA. Recurrent consumer spending declined 1%, better than the guided 3% decline. The company reiterated its full-year net bookings outlook of $8-$8.2 billion, representing ~20% growth, and is confident in the November 19 GTA VI launch. They also raised capex forecast to $290 million due to a real estate purchase and expect to be net cash by year-end.

Gladstone Investment reported Q1 FY2027 adjusted net investment income of $0.26 per share, up from $0.20 in the prior quarter, and total net investment income of $15.9 million ($0.40 per share). The portfolio fair value was $1.3 billion, and the weighted average yield on interest-bearing investments was 12.9%. NAV declined to $16.24 per share due to unrealized depreciation, partly driven by an SFEG valuation adjustment ahead of a pending sale expected to yield a significant capital gain. Management raised the outlook for increased investment activity, with $116 million deployed or committed in the first half, and provided cautious commentary on macroeconomic headwinds.

PPL reported Q2 2026 ongoing EPS of $0.33, a $0.01 increase YoY, and reaffirmed its full-year EPS forecast of $1.90-$1.98 (midpoint $1.94). The company is on pace to deploy ~$5 billion in capital in 2026 and reaffirmed long-term targets including 6%-8% EPS growth through 2029. Pennsylvania rate case settlement effective July 1st, with Rhode Island rates expected September 1st. Data center pipeline in Pennsylvania grew to ~32 GW signed agreements, with over 11 GW under ESAs, and Invitium JV progressing with over 5 GW CCGT reservations.

Canopy Growth reported Q1 FY2027 net revenue of CAD 81.2 million, up 13% year-over-year, with cannabis segment growth of 14% and Storz & Bickel up 6%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 600 basis points to 31% (cannabis segment 26%), and adjusted EBITDA loss improved 59% to CAD 3.2 million. Management reiterated expectations for positive adjusted EBITDA during fiscal 2027 and noted a headwind from Veterans Affairs reimbursement changes, partially mitigated by cost actions. They expect cultivation improvements to impact from late Q2/early Q3.

Spectrum Brands reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 7.7% (organic +6.6%), with all three business units growing and Home & Garden setting a record. Adjusted EBITDA rose 27.5% excluding tariff refunds, and adjusted EPS was $2.79 including a $1.90 refund benefit. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to mid-single-digit growth excluding refunds, while maintaining flat-to-low-single-digit net sales guidance. The company ended the quarter with $258.9 million cash and net leverage of ~1x, and repurchased ~200,000 shares for $15.8 million.

Ready Capital reported Q2 FY2026 GAAP loss from continuing operations of $0.63 per share, improving from a $1.25 loss in Q1, and distributable earnings loss of $0.47 per share (or $0.24 excluding realized losses), versus a $1.33 loss in Q1. Book value per share fell 8.1% to $6.83, a deceleration from prior quarters. Management emphasized progress on liquidity, raising about $1.9 billion and paying down $1.7 billion of debt, and expects to meet 2026 maturities without further large loan sales, relying on financing optimization, runoff, and asset sales. SBA 7 origination volume was $82 million in Q2, well below capacity, but the company expects growth toward a $1.5 billion annual target following a securitization.

RGA reported a record second quarter 2026 with pre-tax adjusted operating income of $761 million or $8.89 per share, driven by strong investment income and favorable claims. New money yield was 6.02% above portfolio yield of 4.96%, and VII returned 15% annualized, well above the 7% plan. Management raised the dividend by 5.4% and affirmed the 8%-10% EPS growth and 13%-15% ROE intermediate-term targets, expressing confidence in meeting or exceeding them.

Ryman Hospitality reported another standout quarter with same-store RevPAR and total RevPAR exceeding expectations by ~2.5 points each, and adjusted EBITDAre outperforming by ~$7 million. Group ADR grew 7.5% YoY, catering contribution per group room night rose nearly 13%, and bookings for future periods hit a record ADR of ~$310. Management raised the midpoints of full-year guidance for same-store hospitality by $10 million and JW Desert Ridge by $1 million, and remains on track for 2027 targets. The entertainment segment posted record adjusted EBITDAre, up nearly 30% YoY.

RLJ Lodging Trust reported Q2 2026 results that significantly exceeded expectations. RevPAR grew 6.8% (ADR +4.9%, occupancy +130 bps to 77%), hotel EBITDA increased 7.1% to $119.5 million with margins up 10 bps (40 bps excluding prior-year tax benefit), and adjusted AFFO per share was $0.52. The company raised full-year guidance due to strong first-half performance and continued momentum, including July RevPAR growth approaching 11%. They also announced the conversion of Key West Fairfield Inn to Compass by Margaritaville, expecting 50% EBITDA upside.

Q2 FY2026 revenue declined 2.7% YoY to $286.7M, slightly better than expected, while adjusted EBITDA fell 3.7% to $76.8M, with margins of 26.8%, an improvement from prior guidance. Adjusted EPS grew 13.2% to $1.03 due to aggressive buybacks. The company completed the sale of its connectivity business for $1.2B, expects to pay ~$200M in taxes and repay $149M in convertible debt, and continues to repurchase stock. AI-authored code roughly doubled and now over half of new code, while Tech & Shopping revenue decline improved to -5% from -13% in Q1.

In Q3 FY2026, Embecta reported total revenue of approximately $272 million, down 8.1% year-over-year on an as-reported basis and 8.9% on an adjusted constant currency basis. Adjusted EPS fell to $0.56 from $1.12 in the prior year, and adjusted operating margin declined to 25.5% from 36.9%. U.S. revenue declined 24.6% year-over-year, while international revenue grew 11.5% on a reported basis. The company reiterated its fiscal 2026 guidance and highlighted the successful close of the Owen Mumford acquisition, which contributed modestly in the quarter. Management noted sequential improvement in revenue and profitability, but cited persistent U.S. headwinds and macro factors such as ACA/Medicaid enrollment and GLP-1 adoption.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 2% to $53.1M, but organic revenue declined 2% due to a $1.8M drop in professional services, concentrated in utilities. Adjusted EBITDA grew 5% to $13.3M, with margin expanding to 25.4%. The company lowered FY2026 guidance materially, citing persistent professional services weakness and slower transaction revenue, and cut FY2027 revenue growth expectations from high-single to mid-single digits. Management expressed confidence in future margin expansion and AI-driven efficiencies, but acknowledged the disappointing quarter.

MDA Space reported Q2 FY2026 revenue up 34% year-over-year to CAD 963 million for the first half, with adjusted EBITDA of CAD 187 million and a 19.4% margin. The company raised its full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoints to CAD 1.85 billion and CAD 350 million, respectively. Book-to-bill was 1.6 times in Q2, and major contract expansions included Telesat Lightspeed (225 satellites, +CAD 474 million), a CSA RADARSAT follow-on (over CAD 600 million), and new defense awards. Two acquisitions (Blue Canyon Technologies and CLS) are expected to close in Q4 2026 and Q4 2026-Q1 2027, respectively, with CLS doubling the recurring revenue base.

Interface reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with currency-neutral net sales up 4% YoY, exceeding expectations, and adjusted EPS of $0.88, up 47%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 524 basis points to 45%, partly from $15.6 million in tariff refunds and operational improvements. Management raised full-year guidance, citing strong order momentum (orders up 5% currency-neutral) and backlog up 22% year-to-date. Healthcare billings grew 19% on top of 28% prior-year growth.

Construction Partners reported a strong Q3 FY2026 with revenue of $999.4 million, up 28.2% year-over-year (8.9% organic, 19.3% acquisitive), adjusted EBITDA of $163 million (up 24%), and adjusted EPS of $1.08. The company raised its fiscal 2026 guidance to reflect over 30% growth in both revenue and bottom-line margins, and highlighted a record backlog. Management expressed confidence in the federal funding outlook and expects strong organic growth in fiscal 2027, with $140 million of acquisitive revenue carrying over.

Post Holdings reported Q3 FY2026 results slightly ahead of expectations, driven by stronger food service performance. Management maintained the midpoint of FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance while narrowing the range. The company repurchased 4% of shares in the quarter, bringing year-to-date reduction to ~17%, but signaled a shift toward debt reduction due to rising interest rates. Preliminary FY2027 adjusted EBITDA outlook is roughly flat versus a comparable base of ~$1.48 billion, facing volume pressure, inflation, and normalized food service earnings. Management also announced closing two peanut butter plants, impacting FY2028, and expects to pursue cost opportunities in pet food as market share stabilizes.

Sun Life reported strong Q2 2026 results with underlying EPS up 13% to CAD 2.02, above their 10% medium-term target, and underlying ROE at 19.1% approaching the 20% target. Record Canada earnings (up 23%), strong Asia growth (up 21%, sales up 20%), and U.S. improvement (underlying up 15%) drove performance. Management raised no guidance but reinforced medium-term targets, noting margin expansion expected in asset management and continued progress in dental and MFS outflows.

Johnson Outdoors reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 5% year-over-year, with operating income of $18.3 million, up $11 million, aided by a one-time $15 million tariff refund. Gross margin improved to 45.3% but would have been modestly lower ex-refunds due to higher raw material costs. The fishing and diving businesses performed well, while camping and watercraft faced weak market conditions. Management noted no additional meaningful tariff refunds expected and cited cost pressures, though year-to-date profitability improved significantly from a prior-year loss.

TDS Telecom delivered record first-half fiber address construction, raising 2026 fiber address guidance but lowering total revenue guidance due to legacy copper/cable pressures. Array grew cash site rental revenue 65% YoY and closed spectrum transactions with T-Mobile and Verizon. Overall adjusted EBITDA guidance was narrowed as legacy declines hit the bottom line, while CapEx guidance was increased to fund accelerated fiber builds.

Sylvamo's Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA roughly doubled sequentially to $60 million, with a 7% margin and adjusted operating earnings of $0.03 per share, but free cash flow remained negative at -$23 million. Management guided to a significant second-half improvement with $75-$85 million benefit from price and mix, but lowered expectations for North American volumes due to Riverdale supply loss and a longer Eastover outage, and cited ongoing Middle East conflict cost pressures. Eastover strategic investments remain on schedule and are expected to generate $55 million in annual benefits by 2027.

Q2 FY2026 revenue fell 3% YoY to $9.7M, with system sales down 34% to $2.3M due to used-device cannibalization and industry distress, while applicator revenue grew 13% YoY and unit volume rose 27% YoY. Gross margin contracted to 76.2% and the company swung to an operating loss of $0.3M, with net loss of $0.7M. Management withdrew FY2026 guidance due to proposed CMS reimbursement cuts for UltraMIST under the PFS rule, though HOPPS proposed rule includes a 14% increase. The company intends to challenge the PFS proposal during the comment period.

Under Armour reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $1.1 billion, down 3% year-over-year, with North America down 9% and APAC down 7% (constant currency down 10%), while EMEA grew 12% and Latin America grew 8%. Adjusted operating income exceeded outlook despite the revenue miss. Management lowered the full-year revenue outlook but maintained adjusted operating income expectations, citing softer consumer demand and a more promotional marketplace. SKU reductions and full-price product launches like the Bouncy Tee were highlighted as progress, though the tone was cautious.

Under Armour reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $1.1 billion, down 3% year-over-year, with North America down 9% and APAC down 7% (or 10% constant currency), while EMEA grew 12% and Latin America grew 8%. Adjusted operating income exceeded expectations despite the revenue miss. Management lowered the full-year revenue outlook as consumer demand softened from late May, especially in North America and Asia Pacific, but maintained adjusted operating income guidance. The company continues its SKU reduction strategy and plans to reduce marketing as a percentage of revenue to improve efficiency.

Nutex Health reported H1 2026 revenue of $427.2M, down 6% YoY, with net income jumping to $112.6M from $3.5M, driven by lower arbitration costs and the HaloMD amendment. Adjusted EBITDA rose 2% to $147.5M and cash flow from operations increased 40% to $109.7M. Q2 same-hospital visits grew 6.3%, but total revenue fell 13.6% due to collection timing and prior-year IDR adjustments. Management is optimistic about legal rulings and the CMS final rule, while in-network progress remains slight. Pipeline expansions are planned for late 2026 and 2027.

In Q2 FY2026, MSDL reported net investment income (NII) of $0.45 per share, down from $0.47 in the prior quarter, and declared a dividend of $0.45 per share. The decline was driven by new non-accruals (three credits added) and higher financing costs, partially offset by Capstone JV accretion. Credit quality remained stable with ~95% of the portfolio risk-rated 2 or better, but non-accruals rose to 2.9% of portfolio at cost. Management expressed confidence in the dividend level and expects the JV to ramp, but acknowledged persistent market headwinds.

Oklo's Q2 FY2026 call highlighted the achievement of first criticality at its Groves isotope facility, reportedly the fastest greenfield-to-criticality transition for a privately funded reactor in history, completed in under a year. Management emphasized an integrated strategy across power, fuel, and isotopes, with progress on Aurora-INL, a planned 1.2 GW Ohio campus, and fuel supply chains. They also noted the DOE Genesis Mission award of $60 million for the Prometheus project and the acquisitions of ARMEC and Creative Engineers to strengthen manufacturing capabilities.

MSC Income Fund reported Q2 FY2026 ANII of $0.33 per share ($0.36 before taxes) and an annualized ROE of 15.9%. NAV per share rose 4% to $16.51, aided by a realized gain of over $11 million from the exit of Centre Technologies. Private loan investments increased net by $10 million to $848 million fair value in 81 companies, with a weighted average yield of 10.4%. Dividends for Q4 total $0.36 per share, and a new $20 million share repurchase plan plus $20 million from Main Street was authorized.

Manitowoc reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $595 million, up 10% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA nearly doubling to $49 million from $26 million, and margin expanding 330 basis points to over 8%. Orders surged 56% to $709 million, backlog rose to $1.05 billion, and net leverage fell to 2.6x. Full-year guidance was raised to $2.3-$2.4 billion sales, $150-$170 million adjusted EBITDA, and $0.80-$1.20 EPS, reflecting a $22.5 million midpoint EBITDA uplift from revenue and tariff refunds. Non-new machine sales reached a record $706 million on a trailing-twelve-month basis, and July orders exceeded $200 million despite seasonality.

NOG reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA up 17% sequentially, free cash flow up over 400% from Q1, and record natural gas volumes up 35% year-over-year. Despite Waha curtailments, the company reiterated capital spend and production guidance, citing cost tailwinds and activity pickup. Management highlighted strong free cash flow of $159 million, a 3% share repurchase, and a raised buyback authorization. They remain confident in asset value, with internal estimates of $7 billion+ versus a $4.6 billion enterprise value.

Matthews International reported a difficult Q3 FY2026 with adjusted EBITDA guidance cut to $158-$162 million, citing engineering order delays, softer memorialization volumes, higher input costs, and Propelis synergy delays. Revenue in Memorialization was $208 million, up 2.1% YoY, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $42.2 million from $42.8 million. The company returned $25 million of Propelis preferred equity and announced a strategic partnership with Linx Printing Technologies, while evaluating strategic alternatives for OLBRICH and expecting DBE-related ramp in 2027.

Wheaton Precious Metals reported record Q2 FY2026 results: production of 202,000 GEOs (up 6% YoY), record revenue of $929M (up 85% YoY), net earnings of $543M (up 86%), and operating cash flow of $650M (up 57%). The quarter included the closing of the $4.3B Antamina silver stream with BHP, the largest streaming deal ever. Management reaffirmed 2026 production guidance of 860,000-940,000 GEOs and the 50% growth target to 1.2M GEOs by 2030. New assets and Antamina contributed, while Salobo grades were lower. Balance sheet remains strong with net debt of ~$1.9B and liquidity of ~$2.6B.

REGENXBIO reported Q2 2026 cash of $106 million, strengthened by a $100 million AbbVie milestone and a $108 million follow-on offering, pro forma cash over $310 million with runway into Q4 2027. Key milestones completed: enrollment in RGX-202 confirmatory study ahead of schedule, FDA alignment on accelerated approval for RGX-121 BLA resubmission, and first patient dosed in NAAVIGATE trial for diabetic retinopathy. BLA submission for RGX-202 initiated in Q3 2026, with top-line wet AMD data from ATMOSPHERE and ASCENT expected in Q4 2026. Management expressed confidence in upcoming data and financial position.

Redwire reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $117.1 million, up 89.6% year-over-year, with record gross margins of 27.8% and backlog of $542.1 million. The company raised substantial capital via ATM, reducing debt and interest expense significantly. Guidance implies continued growth in the second half. Key wins include a NATO Penguin contract, SpaceMD Starfall spacecraft purchase, and new facility expansions.

SandRidge reported record Q2 FY2026 results with revenue up 48% YoY to $51M, adjusted EBITDA up 49% to $34M, and net income of $27M ($0.72/share). Production grew 11% YoY (22% oil growth), driven by higher oil prices and the Cherokee drilling program. The company announced a bolt-on acquisition in the Cherokee Play, continues to pay dividends, and maintains a strong balance sheet with no debt. Guidance for 2026 remains intact with $76-97M capex and 10 wells planned.

AVITA Medical reported Q2 2026 revenue of $21.7 million, up 18% year-over-year and 13% sequentially, exceeding $20 million for the first time. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $86-89 million (20-24% growth) and introduced new guidance to achieve cash flow breakeven in Q4 2026. Gross margin improved to 81.9%, operating loss narrowed to $6.9 million, and net cash use improved to $3.2 million. RECELL U.S. volumes grew over 10% sequentially to 2,600 units, with strong RECELL GO mini adoption in smaller wounds, and CMS has proposed 2027 RVUs for new Category 1 CPT codes.

Star Bulk reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $1.21 and adjusted EBITDA of $184.2 million, with a daily cash margin of $17,944. The company declared a $0.09 per share dividend and continues to return 100% of operating cash flow. Management highlighted strong cash generation, low leverage (net debt at 50% of demolition value), and ongoing fleet rejuvenation with new Kamsarmax deliveries, while noting expectations for Simandou volumes to ramp from 15-20 million tons in 2026 to 120 million by 2029.

StandardAero's Q2 2026 showed revenue up 4.6% to $1.6B, adjusted EBITDA up 12.3% to $230M with record 14.4% margin, and adjusted EPS up 24% to $0.40. Both LEAP and CFM56 DFW programs reached profitability, and the company raised full-year guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS. CRS segment margin declined 270bps on timing issues but is expected to recover in H2. A new $180M license expansion is expected to add ~$25M annual EBITDA over the next few years.

The Real Brokerage reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $700.6 million, up 30% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $27.6 million, up 38% year-over-year. Despite a challenging housing market, closed transactions rose 27% to a record 62,380. The company reaffirmed its pending RE/MAX transaction, expecting to complete it in H2 2026 and targeting $30 million in cost synergies within three years. Guidance indicates Q3 sequential declines due to seasonality, with combined company guidance planned for the Q3 call.

Radian reported Q2 2026 with total revenues of $575 million, up 93% year-over-year, driven by the Inigo acquisition, and net earned premiums up 116% to $504 million. Adjusted net operating EPS grew to $1.14, with adjusted net operating ROE of 13%. Mortgage segment new insurance written rose 14% to $16.3 billion, and persistency improved to 82%. Specialty net premiums earned increased 9% to $267 million, with plans for second-half earned premiums to be about 20% higher than first-half. Guidance for full-year share repurchases was raised to the upper end of the $200-250 million range, and expected Radian Guaranty dividends increased to $650 million or more. Market conditions in specialty insurance are more competitive, and a $30 million Middle East reserve was established.

Sabre's Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 4% to $712 million, with normalized adjusted EBITDA up 19% to $151 million, exceeding guidance. Full-year pro forma adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to approximately $600 million and free cash flow to -$65 million. Air distribution bookings grew 1%, ahead of expectations, with noted resilience in corporate volumes and ongoing impacts from Middle East conflict and fuel prices. The company reported strong growth in hotel revenue, payments gross spend, and NDC, while highlighting agentic AI progress with doubling of active partners to 60.

Rayonier reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.10 and adjusted EBITDA of $124 million, driven by PotlatchDeltic contributions and strong segment performance. Southern and Northwest Timber EBITDA rose significantly year-over-year, while Wood Products posted its best quarter since 2022. The company completed a tax-efficient land exchange with RMS, repurchased $72 million of shares, and affirmed full-year guidance with stable to higher lumber pricing trends.

Q2 FY2026 GMV hit an all-time high of $617 million, up 22% YoY (fourth consecutive quarter above 20%), with revenue up 17% to $193 million. Adjusted EBITDA reached $13.5 million (7% margin), expanding 290 bps YoY and beating prior guidance. Active buyers rose 11% to 1.1 million, and the company raised its full-year revenue and EBITDA outlook while guiding Q3 GMV to $610-620 million. Management highlighted Athena automation, AI pricing, and high-value item growth as key drivers.

Revenue surged 115% YoY to $451 million with record operating cash flow of $335 million, up 119%. Adjusted EPS rose 41% to $2.56. Guidance for gold and silver is tracking well; copper and other metals trending around or above top end. Management noted strong portfolio diversification and progress simplifying Sandstorm assets.

RXO reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.8 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $40 million (above the high end of guidance), and adjusted EPS of $0.06. Brokerage volume grew 2% YoY, with truckload spot mix up 900 bps sequentially to 42% and truckload gross profit per load up 11% sequentially, the largest gain in four years. Last mile stops grew 3%, and managed transportation won ~$100 million in freight under management. Management guided to continued brokerage volume and gross profit per load growth in Q3, but expects weakening in last mile. Free cash flow was -$42 million due to working capital, expected to convert strongly in Q3.

Republic Services reported Q2 FY2026 revenue growth of 4.6% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 4.5%, with adjusted EPS of $1.85. The company maintained adjusted EBITDA margin at 32.1% despite headwinds from prior-year landfill event volumes. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance across revenue, adjusted EBITDA, EPS, and free cash flow, citing higher fuel recovery fee revenue, increased recycling commodity prices, and acquisitions. Volume declined 1.6% on total revenue due to tough comps, but underlying pricing exceeded cost inflation and management expects sequential volume improvement.

Relmada reported Q2 2026 results with no revenue, a net loss of $12.9M ($0.11 per share) compared to $9.9M ($0.30) in the prior year, and cash of $217.7M expected to fund operations through 2029. Management reiterated plans to file NDV-01 IND by year-end 2026 and initiate the phase III rescue program, while noting manufacturing is the final critical step and sepranolone IND is also targeted for year-end. Guidance for first phase III data was pushed to likely first half of 2027, with management emphasizing the need for a meaningful patient count before disclosure.

Ring Energy reported Q2 2026 production of 19,990 BOE/d, up 3% sequentially, with realized oil prices up 38% to $95.45/barrel, but hedges limited upside. The company completed an equity offering, reducing debt to about $360 million and leverage to 1.7 times. Management raised second-half 2026 oil sales guidance midpoint by about 2% and lowered LOE midpoint guidance slightly, while increasing full-year 2026 capital spending to $158-$178 million. Initial 2027 guidance shows BOE volume growth of about 10% and a ~10% midpoint reduction in capital spending.

BRC Group reported Q2 2026 net income of $18.5 million and operating adjusted EBITDA of $66 million, the best core operating quarter in nearly three years. Total revenues were $239 million, up $14 million year-over-year, driven by a $30 million increase in management fees from carried interest in SpaceX funds. The company reduced total debt by $497 million since December 2024 to $1.277 billion, with net debt down $87 million to $285 million. Management highlighted reactivated institutional accounts, a strong capital markets pipeline, and expects to comfortably cover $306 million in upcoming senior note maturities with cash and investments.

Riley Exploration Permian reported Q2 FY2026 with oil production near the high end of guidance, 5% sequential growth, and a June exit rate of 24.4 thousand barrels per day. The company raised full-year oil production guidance to ~30% year-over-year growth, with Q3 expected to be up >20% sequentially. Midstream constraints in April-May reduced oil production by ~2,000 barrels per day, but new Targa pipeline is expected in early Q4 2026. Full-year CapEx guidance was increased by 12% at the midpoint, and free cash flow declined to $6 million in Q2 due to higher capital spend.

Transocean beat its Q2 FY2026 guidance on revenue and cost, with revenue of $966 million at the upper end of the range and adjusted EBITDA margin of 32%. Fleet uptime hit 98%, and backlog grew by about $300 million excluding a pending $1 billion Equinor award. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance, expects to close the Valaris acquisition in Q4, and plans to call $200 million of 8% notes, reducing gross debt to below $4.8 billion.

Rigetti reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $5.1M, up from $1.8M a year earlier, driven by on-premises Novera QPU sales. Gross margin improved to 43% from 31%, while GAAP net loss widened to $52.6M due to non-cash warrant and earn-out fair value adjustments; non-GAAP net loss was $16M or $0.05 per diluted share. The company highlighted technical progress, a $100M CHIPS Act letter of intent, and expanded HPE/Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center collaboration, with guidance expectations for the remainder of the year referenced but not fully quantified in the transcript excerpt.

In Q2 FY2026, Rocket Companies delivered adjusted revenue of $2.8 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $766 million (28% margin, up from 26% in Q1), and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.16, its most profitable quarter in four years despite a challenging spring market. The company achieved record market share in both purchase (6.2%) and refinance (14.3%), and is executing ahead of plan on the Redfin and Mr. Cooper integrations. Management emphasized a diversified revenue base, with over 70% of revenue recurring or less rate-sensitive, and expressed confidence in long-term earnings power.

Planet Fitness reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $365 million, up 7% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA up 3.5%. System-wide same club sales increased 1.7%, entirely driven by rate, with Black Card penetration up 210 bps to ~68%. Membership reached 21.5 million, up 3.6% year-over-year but flat sequentially; attrition at 3.5%. The company reiterated its guidance with no negative comp quarters expected in Q3 or Q4, but noted the marketing initiatives will take time to gain traction.

Red Cat reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $20.2 million, up 520% year-over-year, with gross margin improving to 16.1% from 11.6% a year ago and 12.7% sequentially. Management highlighted continued scaling, new product introductions (Hellcat, Blue Ops Variant 7), and strong demand, expecting a 'dramatic' revenue ramp in Q3 and Q4. Cash stood at $325.6 million, and they reaffirmed a focus on profitability in 2027.

In Q2 2026, RBI reported 3.8% same-store sales growth, 6.7% organic Adjusted Operating Income growth, and 12.9% Adjusted EPS growth, with Burger King US delivering an exceptional 8.6% same-store sales, beating the industry by over nine points. Tim Hortons was flat, Popeyes declined 5.2%, but International grew 5.5%, and Firehouse grew 0.4%. The company reiterated its 2026 algorithm and expects improving momentum, with Popeyes returning to positive comps in H2 and Burger King's elevation driving sustained outperformance, though beef costs remain a near-term headwind.

Park-Ohio reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $440 million, up 10% year-over-year, with record revenues in Supply Technologies and Engineered Products. Adjusted EPS rose 24% to $0.93, and operating income increased 22% year-over-year. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance for net sales to $1.7-1.73 billion and adjusted EPS to $3.10-3.30, citing strong demand across multiple end markets. Management also noted strong backlogs and continued operational improvements, while reviewing strategic alternatives for Southwest Steel Processing, which is expected to be a drag this year.

Pulse Biosciences reported Q2 FY2026 results, highlighting significant progress in its nPulse cardiac catheter pivotal study, which surpassed halfway enrollment ahead of schedule and is expected to complete in early October, three months earlier than originally planned. The company raised $57.5 million in net proceeds through an ATM program, ending the quarter with over $100 million cash on hand, and amended its study protocol to increase enrollment target to 164 patients. Vybrance disposable sales rose sequentially to $434,000 from $400,000. Management expressed confidence in the technology's differentiated efficacy and workflow advantages, and announced a partnership with the Clayman Thyroid Center.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was $731.1 million, up 5% YoY but down 1.8% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA was $206.1 million with a 28.2% margin, up from 16.8% in Q1. D2C revenue grew 63.1% YoY to reach 39.3% of revenue. Management maintained full-year guidance but expects to land near the lower end, citing deliberate front-loaded marketing spend reduction and softening consumer demand. Disney Solitaire revenue grew 15.5% sequentially despite lower marketing spend, but management expects sequential revenue declines in the second half due to spend timing.

Progyny reported record Q2 2026 revenue, gross profit, and adjusted EBITDA, with revenue up 5.3% reported and 11% excluding a former client's transition agreement. Gross margin expanded 180 basis points year-over-year. Management highlighted strong watching season momentum with early commitments ahead of last year and retention de-risked for 2027, reiterating the target of adding 1 million or more lives. The company announced a new $200 million share repurchase program and continued to generate strong cash flow, with over $50 million in operating cash flow for the fourth time in five quarters.

Q2 2026 showed strong results with revenue up 35.8% to $298M and adjusted EBITDA up 48.2% to $24.3M, driven by acquisitions and operational excellence. Adjusted EPS rose 33.3% to $0.36. Management raised full-year guidance, citing momentum and better-than-expected acquisition transitions. Home health and hospice segments delivered strong same-store growth, while senior living showed stable improvements.

PENN reported record Q2 retail revenues of $1.5 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $517.2 million, up 4% and 6% year-over-year, respectively. Interactive segment revenue was $349.4 million with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $9.5 million, improving year-over-year. The company raised full-year retail revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $5.87 billion and $1.963 billion at the midpoint, while fine-tuning interactive revenue guidance down to $1.57 billion and reiterating an interactive adjusted EBITDA loss of $20 million. Management highlighted strong development project performance, balance sheet improvements, and a disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Permian Resources reported record Q2 free cash flow of $751 million, up nearly 50% quarter-over-quarter, and record FCF per share of $0.88. Oil production increased 3% sequentially to about 198,000 bbl/day, helped by a 50% increase in workover rigs and higher working interest (82% vs original 75% expectations). Full-year oil production guidance was raised to 199,000 bbl/day (10% above 2025), while CapEx midpoint is $1.95 billion, about 1% lower than last year. Management highlighted aggressive year-to-date acquisitions of about 55,000 net acres for ~$1.05 billion, with leverage at 0.5x.

Palladyne AI reported record Q2 2026 revenue of approximately $5.8M, up 63% sequentially, with backlog increasing to $25M from $17M. The company reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $24M-$27M and expects cash burn to decline in the second half. Management highlighted successful field exercises, contract awards, and broad-based momentum across business units.

PRA Group reported Q2 2026 cash collections of $559 million, up 4% year-over-year, and total revenues up 29% to $372 million. Net income was $58 million. The company increased European ERC by $349 million due to over-performance, and highlighted continued cost discipline with 135 roles eliminated and $20 million annualized savings. Management raised no explicit guidance but signaled improved forecasting and record ERC of $8.9 billion.

PDF Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $61.5 million, up 19% year-over-year, with first-half revenues up 22%. Backlog grew to $271 million, up 10% sequentially and 16% year-over-year, driven by multiple eight-figure contracts (secureWISE and DirectScan) and record Cimetrix bookings. Gross margin was 73%, down sequentially due to higher perpetual licenses in Q1, but management expects expansion toward the 77% target. The company reaffirmed 20% full-year revenue growth guidance, despite increased CapEx for eProbe tools.

Praxis reported Q2 FY2026 with two NDAs in late-stage FDA review for ulixacaltamide and relutrigine. Mid-cycle meetings showed no advisory committee plans and no findings from BIMO inspections. Operating expenses rose to $96.9M and cash ended at $1.4B. The vormatrigine POWER1 study missed primary endpoints but met a key secondary endpoint, with plans to amend POWER2/POWER3.

PureCycle reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $4.5 million, up substantially year-over-year, with production of 4.5 million pounds of PureFive and about 5 million pounds of feedstock processed. The company completed a major turnaround ahead of schedule and below budget, set a new daily throughput record in June, and brought compounding in-house. Management reiterated the second-half Ironton breakeven target, citing accelerated customer qualifications following New Jersey's approval of PureFive as recycled content and commercial production of Procter & Gamble's Downy caps, with Tide caps and Vicks ZzzQuil lids scheduled for Q3 and Q4.

PAR Technology reported Q2 FY2026 with ARR of $338 million, up over 17% year-over-year and 12.3% organic, and adjusted EBITDA of $14.3 million, beating the prior guidance range of $9.5-$11.5 million even excluding a $1.3 million one-off hardware project. The company highlighted nearly 100% multi-product attachment on new deals, six PAR Ordering wins, and PAR Intelligence reaching roughly 20,000 restaurant sites, with 17,000 retail sites. Management raised the full-year outlook, citing strong pipeline and deployment momentum, and remains confident in accelerating ARR growth in the second half.

Occidental reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.40, with production of 1.43 million BOE/d, exceeding the midpoint of guidance by 23,000 BOE/d. Free cash flow was approximately $3 billion, the highest since Q3 2022, and midstream and marketing set a new record with adjusted earnings of about $960 million. The company reduced principal debt to $11.8 billion, raised the dividend by 8%, and reaffirmed a plan to add over $4 billion of annual sustainable cash flow by 2030, with approximately 85% achievable at lower prices. Guidance reflects expectations for normalized Waha/Gulf Coast spreads partially offset by upstream price improvements, while Middle East disruptions could impact sulfur sales and freight costs.

Perdoceo reported Q2 2026 net income of $48 million ($0.75 per diluted share), up from $41 million ($0.62) a year ago, with revenue rising 1.8% to $213.4 million. Adjusted operating income grew 4.4% to $64.2 million and adjusted EPS increased 19.4% to $0.80. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted operating income guidance to $258-$263 million and adjusted EPS to $3.10-$3.16, while boosting the quarterly dividend by 13.3% to $0.17. Enrollments grew 0.7% overall, with CTU up 0.6% for an 11th consecutive quarter, AIU down 1% due to Trident, and St. Augustine up 6%.

Ouster delivered record Q2 2026 revenue of $55 million, up 56% year-over-year, with over 17,000 sensors shipped, marking the 14th consecutive quarter of product revenue growth. GAAP gross margin was 49%, aided by a one-time refund of ~1,000 basis points, while Adjusted EBITDA improved to -$4 million. Q3 revenue guidance of $54.5-57.5 million implies a slight sequential decline as Rev8 ramps to production, and full-year guidance remains unchanged. The company raised substantial capital, ending the quarter with $263 million in cash and no debt, and subsequently raised ~$191 million net, which management says fully funds its operating plan.

OTF reported Q2 2026 adjusted NII of $0.30 per share, stable NAV of $16.48, and non-accruals at 10 basis points, among the lowest in the industry. Net leverage rose to 0.93x, near the low end of the target range, and the company completed $500 million unsecured bond, $150 million secured facility, and extended its revolver. Management expects to cover the base dividend by mid-next year and continues repurchasing shares, with $195 million still available. The investment environment has improved with wider spreads, and management remains confident in portfolio quality despite slower technology deal activity.

Oscar Health reported Q2 2026 revenue of $4.9 billion, up 70% year-over-year, with MLR improving to 79.2% and SG&A expense ratio at a record low of 14.2%. Earnings from operations surged to $389 million, and net income was $362 million, both up sharply year-over-year. The company raised full-year 2026 earnings from operations guidance to $500-700 million, up $250 million, and improved MLR guidance to 81.5%-82.5%. Management highlighted favorable risk adjustment and utilization trends but remained cautious on CMS program integrity-driven member churn in the second half.

Primerica reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted operating revenues up 8% YoY and adjusted net operating income up 11%, with adjusted operating EPS up 17% to $6.41 including a $0.15 tax benefit. The ISP segment grew revenues 21% and pre-tax income 31%, with record AUM of $140 billion and $397 million in net inflows. Term Life premiums grew 3.4% but issued policies declined 12%, and the company guided full-year issued policies down mid-single digits. Management raised ISP sales guidance to 10%-15% growth for 2026, while maintaining full-year expense growth of 7%-8%.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was CAD 2.5 million, up 12% year-over-year, but was impacted by CAD 3.1 million of TULSA shipments delayed to July; excluding that, revenue would have been ~CAD 5.6 million, representing 153% growth. Gross margin rose to 78%, net loss narrowed to CAD 9.5 million, and cash stood at CAD 38.3 million. Management maintained full-year 2026 revenue guidance of ~CAD 25 million (56% growth), citing record order activity and a qualified pipeline of ~CAD 70 million. Reimbursement tailwinds include a proposed 14.9% Medicare payment increase for TULSA and expansion of covered lives by 18.3 million in Q2, with Johns Hopkins and Prime Healthcare employer plans newly covering TULSA.

Privia Health reported strong Q2 results: practice collections grew 12.4% to $970 million, adjusted EBITDA increased 29% to $37.4 million with margin expanding 310 bps to 28.3% of care margin. Implemented providers grew 10.1% and attributed lives grew 19.2%. The company raised its 2026 guidance across most metrics, citing strong first-half performance. Management remains confident in long-term growth and margin expansion, despite minor CMS cash timing delays.

In Q2 FY2026, Power Solutions International reported net sales of $152.5 million, up 18.6% sequentially from Q1, exceeding expectations, but down 21% year-over-year due to softer oil and gas demand and shipment timing. Gross margin improved sequentially by 420 basis points to 27.1%, driven by operational improvements at Wisconsin, though year-over-year it declined from 28.2%. Operating cash flow was strong at $56.6 million, enabling $30.8 million debt reduction. Management expects H2 2026 sales to exceed H1, roughly in line with H2 2025, but provided no formal guidance due to order timing variability and continued oil and gas softness.

PubMatic reported a strong Q2, returning to double-digit revenue growth well ahead of schedule, with expectations for acceleration in the second half. The company highlighted leadership in agentic advertising with over 80 agentic campaigns, up from 30 a quarter ago, and new initiatives like Decision Fabric. CFO Steve Pantelick announced retirement but remains through Q1 2027 and in advisory role until July 2027. Guidance likely raised or reaffirmed with accelerating growth, though exact figures are not provided in the excerpt. The company sees political advertising as a tailwind in Q3 and Q4.

Papa John's Q2 2026 North America comps declined 8.3% while international comps grew 1.5%; total performance pressured by softer consumer and heavy QSR discounting. Management revised 2026 guidance to global system-wide sales decline of 2%-4% and adjusted EBITDA of $180-$190 million, including an incremental $18 million investment. Transformation is taking longer than expected; management announced leadership changes and expects 200-250 of planned closures to occur in 2026.

D-Wave reported expanding commercial momentum with new and expanded customer engagements (AT&T, Optum, NTT) and a Nature-published validation of its dual-rail gate model architecture. The company reiterated its roadmap: 17 physical qubit system by end of 2025, 49 qubit in 2026, 181 qubit in 2028, 10 logical qubits by 2030, and 100 logical qubits by 2032. Management guided to roughly 2-3 annealing system sales per year at $20M-$40M each, with revenue recognized over two quarters per system. No specific financial figures for revenue, EPS, or margins were provided in the transcript excerpt.

Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 2% constant currency, with ex-China growth of 6%; adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to $129 million with margin up 310 bps to 20%. China revenue declined 23% and respiratory season is expected to be soft, leading to guidance cuts for FY2026 revenue ($2.52B-$2.60B), adjusted EBITDA ($540M-$560M), and adjusted EPS ($0.65-$0.90). Free cash flow guidance was withdrawn, and operating cash flow was negative $111 million for the quarter.

Qiagen reported Q2 2026 net sales of $535 million, flat at CER, beating guidance for a ~2% decline, and adjusted EPS of $0.62, above the outlook of at least $0.60. Growth pillars grew 5% CER, with Sample Technologies up 9% and QIAcuity double-digit, but PCR was down 8% and QIAstat-Dx fell 7% on respiratory comparison. The company reaffirmed full-year guidance of 1-2% CER growth and EPS of at least $2.43, expecting second-half growth to improve to 3-4% CER. Operating income margin contracted to 29.4% from 29.9%, and the dividend was raised 40% to $0.35.

Solaris reported record Q2 2026 with revenue of ~$219M, up 12% sequentially, and adjusted EBITDA of ~$108M, up 30% sequentially, with adjusted pro forma EPS of $0.39. The company raised Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $90M-$105M and introduced Q4 guidance of $100M-$120M, reflecting GESA acquisition and new contract ramps. Management highlighted multiple contract expansions with three investment-grade tech customers, a new nuclear SMR investment, and strong demand with multiple gigawatts in active negotiations.

In Q2 FY2026, TripAdvisor's continuing operations (experiences and hotels) reported revenue of $442M and adjusted EBITDA of $76M, with revenue in line and EBITDA above expectations. Experiences bookings grew 5% overall, with Viator up 10%, but TripAdvisor POS faced SEO headwinds (~5 pts of growth drag). Hotels revenue declined 21% due to sustained volume headwinds. Management announced the sale of TheFork for $700M, expects to close before year-end, and reiterated long-term confidence in experiences while remaining cautious on macro and Q3 guidance.

Serve Robotics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.2 million, up 9% sequentially and over 400% YoY, but below expectations due to a decline in Uber delivery volume. The company materially lowered full-year revenue guidance from $26 million to $9-$10 million, citing the removal of assumed second-half growth from Uber. Management says the Uber agreement may not be renewed in early 2027 and is reallocating resources to diversified channels, including DoorDash (up ~50% sequentially), advertising (~50% of robot delivery revenue), and hospital robotics. Gross margin was -271% with a gross loss of ~$8.8 million, but fleet gross margin improved sequentially.

Peloton delivered Q4 FY2026 revenue of $608M, slightly above guidance, with gross margin up 260bps to 56.7%. Adjusted EBITDA was $142M (or $166M excluding one-time legal contingencies), above guidance, and FY2026 marked the first full year of positive net income ($63M) and operating income ($161M). Management projects record gross margin, EBITDA, and net income in FY2027, while expecting churn to be roughly flat year-over-year. The company is also executing a balance-sheet refinancing and plans new consumer product launches in fall 2027.

WaterBridge reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $217.8 million (up 8% sequentially) and Adjusted EBITDA of $115.8 million (up ~12% sequentially), with Adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 53%. Management raised full-year 2026 volume and Adjusted EBITDA guidance for the second consecutive quarter and raised CapEx guidance by $100 million to $530-$590 million. The quarter included the closing of the Ranger acquisition, announcement of the NDB Landfill acquisition, and acceleration of the New Devon project. Speedway Phase I launched on schedule in July with volumes expected to ramp toward ~100,000 barrels per day and exit the year above that.

Walker & Dunlop's Q2 FY2026 core business grew modestly with transaction volumes up 3% to $14.4 billion and adjusted core EPS up 3% to $1.19, but reported diluted EPS was $0.09 due to $23 million in charges related to fraudulent loan repurchases. Management confirmed Freddie Mac's investigation is complete and expects $12-16 million additional charges in Q3 for Fannie Mae, with no further repurchases expected. Guidance for the year was not formally revised but management expressed confidence in core earnings excluding these charges, with GSE market share up to 15% and $114 billion in remaining GSE capacity.

Weave reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $67.5 million, up 15.5% year over year, with payments revenue growing roughly double that rate. The company added record gross and net new locations, especially in dental, and expanded adjusted operating margin to nearly 5%, up from roughly breakeven a year ago. However, management noted a go-to-market transition led to bookings slightly below expectations, reflected in the revenue outlook. CEO expressed strong optimism about demand and AI-driven monetization opportunities.

ResMed reported Q4 FY2026 revenue growth of 8% constant currency, non-GAAP EPS up 16%, and gross margin expansion. For FY2026, they achieved 10% headline revenue growth, 180bps operating margin expansion, and over $1.6 billion in free cash flow. They announced a 10% dividend increase, accelerated buybacks, and raised FY2027 guidance that beats consensus. The company also closed the Noctrix acquisition, plans to divest MatrixCare, and reaffirmed tariff relief for their products.

QuinStreet reported record Q4 FY2026 with revenue up 43% YoY to $373.9M and adjusted EBITDA up 87% to $41.4M, driving margin expansion.
